subject.title: Codex app-server stall (item/completed, no turn/completed, recovery=none) still occurs on stable 2026.6.11; corroborates logs_2.sqlite bloat root cause (refs #84076 #89974 #71127)

question: Should OpenClaw prioritize a fresh latest-version reproduction and user-visible recovery hardening, while treating `logs_2.sqlite` retention as an upstream Codex defect unless a plugin-owned lifecycle seam is demonstrated?
rationale: The issue combines an OpenClaw recovery symptom with a likely upstream Codex storage/performance concern; choosing an OpenClaw timeout or storage policy before reproducing current behavior could either abort legitimate work or duplicate the upstream fix.

options.title: Reproduce then split ownership
options.body: Recommended: validate the incident on v2026.7.1/current main, harden only proven OpenClaw lane recovery, and link upstream Codex evidence for log retention.

options.title: Add an OpenClaw mitigation
options.body: Add a narrowly documented operator-facing mitigation only if current evidence shows the bundled plugin safely owns the Codex-home lifecycle and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Treat it as upstream-only
options.body: Close local recovery work only after a current-version trace proves OpenClaw already releases the lane and surfaces the failed turn correctly.

recommendation.title: Reproduce then split ownership
recommendation.body: Recommended: validate the incident on v2026.7.1/current main, harden only proven OpenClaw lane recovery, and link upstream Codex evidence for log retention.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex and recovery work makes this the strongest available routing signal for the boundary decision.
